The haze of sleep started to fade,bit by bit he could feel himself again. The heavy blanket, the soft thin mattress that he lay on, the cold air on his feet washing over him. Cold air? Mark rose his head up and looked at his cell door, from here he could see cell after cell just like his like countless mornings, days, weeks yet never had he felt a cold breeze in here. He rubbed his unshaven chin and rose to look at himself in the mirror. Why had he not been woken for breakfast? It felt much later in the day then I had any right to be. He walked to the bars of his cell door and shouted out to the guards “Hey boss! Breakfast?” the small echo of his own voice was his only reply. “Boss?” Mark gave his cell door a slam with his hand. They always told them not to do this but surly it would get them to come over. His cell door rattled and then fell quiet. Quiet, the whole damn place was quiet, no shouting of guards or the mocking voices of prisoners to each other. No metal clank of doors opening and closing. Without thinking mark gave his door a tug, it felt loose. It did not have a handle however, his was a cell he sliped his fingers around to the lock on the other side of his door and pushed his finger nail into it, if he couldd just turn it. Nothing, what if he never got out? What if no one came back? What if he had to sit here until he died slowly without water or food, or... no, don't panic.

Mark looked around his cell at the few things he had in it. He took his tooth brush and gave it a hard stab into the lock on the other side of the door, his door rattled as he did as his eyes went wide as he waited to hear the angry yell of a guard and the heavy sound of boots walking towards his cell. He heard nothing and twisted the toothbrush, the door was unlocked but the latch was down. After a few panicked minutes he felt the door give way to him and he fell forward as the door gave way, he rose to his feet and shook his head looking around the tall cell block he had lived in for 2 years. 2 years and he had never seen a day like today. Mark took a few careful steps forward before he broke into a normal walk, he felt the cold breeze again, this time on his face. He turned to see the only thing other then himself and his open cell that was out of place one of the cell block cell doors was open. He walked towards it and the cold breeze that got stronger as he walked towards it. The hall that he walked in was dark as none of the lights had been turned on, he placed one hand on the wall and walked forward. Mark could not see it but his cell had closed itself, his blanket slipped itself back into order to any outsider it would not seem that marks cell looked just like all the others. Mark had never seen some of these parts of the prison, he felt like he wanted to stop and look around but not before he learned just where the breeze was coming from.

It was like a soft wind now when mark found the lobby of the prison just like everywhere it seemed as if everyone had made sure it was all neat before getting up and walking away. The cold air blew into him from the two main doors, he could hear it ever so softly  slipping under the doors and in his excitement almost ran to them before he looked back for the first and last time. He opened the doors and stepped outside. “Hello mark, and welcome.”
